messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] High rate of TLS handshake failures detected (prod-eu, prod-us) — 5m spike. Triggers: api-gateway, edge-lb. Severity: P1 if sustained. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tls-networking

Samir Shah: Ack. I see 502/504 uptick in synthetic checks and customer error reports. Pulling LB logs.

Elena Novak: landing LB log sample — pattern shows 'tls: unknown certificate' and 'alert 20' in the handshake. snippet:
```
2026-03-18T11:02:10Z edge-lb-02 tls: handshake error: tls: unknown certificate
2026-03-18T11:02:11Z edge-lb-05 tls: TLS alert 20: unexpected message
```

Ravi Menon: any recent cert ops? I see a cert-rotation job kicked off at 11:00Z: job id cert-rot-2026-03-18-1100. Automation logs show several retries to edge-lb-05 with 'connection reset by peer'.

Samir Shah: rotation log excerpt:
```
[11:00:02Z] cert-rot: start cert-rot-2026-03-18-1100
[11:00:12Z] push -> edge-lb-02 OK
[11:00:14Z] push -> edge-lb-05 ERROR: write tcp 10.2.7.5:443: connection reset by peer
[11:00:17Z] retry push -> edge-lb-05 OK
[11:00:25Z] cert-rot: completed with warnings
```

Elena Novak: running `openssl s_client -connect edge-lb-02:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts` shows intermediate chain A. edge-lb-05 shows intermediate chain B. So endpoints are inconsistent.

Ravi Menon: inconsistent chain + RST during push -> two potential failure modes: 1) partial chain deployment (clients reject mixed chain) 2) network path issues cause truncated TLS records leading to handshake alert. We need data: tcpdumps from edge-lb-02/05 and path MTU.

Samir Shah: collecting pcaps now. starting tcpdump on edge-lb-05 and edge-lb-02 (capture ClientHello and ServerHello). tcpdump filter: `tcp port 443 and (tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-push != 0)`

ops-bot: pagerduty: oncall rota: Elena Novak oncall acknowledged.

Elena Novak: I have pcaps uploaded to the incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-2026-445/pcaps. Quick grep shows large ClientHello fragmented across 2 segments and server replies with TLS alert 40. Also tracepath from orchestrator to edge-lb-05 shows pmtu 1400 on intermediate hop.

Ravi Menon: that 1400 PMTU is suspicious. Some TLS stacks with larger ClientHello + SNI/OCSP stapling may exceed a single segment. If DF set, packet gets dropped or fragmented leading to handshake error on some clients.

Samir Shah: mitigations: A) push full_cert_chain to all LBs to ensure uniform chain B) re-run cert-rotate with stronger retry/backoff or push via mux host C) enable MSS clamping on edge routers to reduce segmentation issues. Which do we do now?

Elena Novak: I'll do MSS clamp first since it's quick and non-intrusive. Command to push to routers: `netctl apply --profile mss-clamp-1400 edge-router-*`. Doing that now.

Ravi Menon: I'll prepare a full-chain push: `certctl deploy --bundle /opt/certs/2026-03-18/full_chain.pem --targets edge-lb-* --force-reload`. Can run after MSS clamp.

[~11:12Z] Elena Novak: MSS clamp applied to edge-router-1/2/3. Monitor shows reduced fragmentation signals.

[~11:15Z] Samir Shah: initiating full-chain push now. streaming logs:
- deploy -> edge-lb-02 OK
- deploy -> edge-lb-05 OK
- deploy -> edge-lb-01 OK

Elena Novak: synthetic checks starting to pass. error spikes dropping from ~18% of requests to ~3% in 10m. customer reports decreasing.

Ravi Menon: adding timeline entries to INC-2026-445 ticket and documenting hypotheses: H1 partial cert chain due to rotation retry; H2 MTU fragmentation causing truncated ClientHello; H3 bad intermediary CA pushed. Evidence: openssl shows mixed intermediates -> supports H1; tracepath and pcap shows fragmentation -> supports H2; no CA-wide revocation seen -> lower probability for H3.

Samir Shah: for RCA follow-ups: 1) make cert-rot require post-deploy validation (verify uniform chain via s_client) before marking success 2) add PMTU checks pre-rotation or use control path with MSS clamping for rotations 3) increase cert-rotate idempotency / use staged rollouts with canary checks

ops-bot: note: next oncall handover in 20m.

Elena Novak: I'm taking the remainder of the incident. Samir -> please leave any remaining logs in the ticket. I'll prepare a customer-safe status update in 15m: brief, non-technical.

Samir Shah: posted customer-safe note draft: "We experienced intermittent TLS connection failures affecting some API traffic due to an automated certificate update combined with network path MTU differences. We applied mitigations and the service is recovering. A full RCA will be shared."

Ravi Menon: filing automation task: AUT-1326 add post-push chain validation + abort on mismatch. Also AUT-1327: make cert-rotate tolerant of transient connection resets and use alternate delivery path.

Elena Novak: monitoring window started. leaving detailed pcap and logs attached.

pagerduty: INC-2026-445 acknowledged, status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Samir Shah: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem doc and link to proposed automation PRs. Leaving channel (ending shift).

Elena Novak: copying final notes into RCA ticket and will coordinate postmortem. closing incident coordination thread here.
